As shown in the output above, the new VHOST entry is preprod-payroll.trick.htb.

Browsing to preprod-payroll.trick.htb returns the following webpage:

Default credentials do not work. However, I bypassed the login page using SQL injection:

The payload injected is inside the username field:

admin' OR '1'='1'-- -
admin' OR '1'='1'-- -

Looking through the Users page, I notice an entry with the username Enemigosss:

After pressing the drop-down button and then Edit, I right-clicked on the password field, and pressed Reveal Password to get the password SuperGucciRainbowCake:

However, the credentials does not seem to work.

After intercepting the login request and using sqlmap to test for SQL injection, I notice it is being run as reno:

As shown in the output above, there is another hostname preprod-marketing.trick.htb.

After adding the new hostname to the /etc/hosts file and accessing the website, I notice the parameter page is used to include files:

When checking for file inclusion vulnerabilities, I get a hit as I am able to read the /etc/passwd file on the server:

Since the target is running Nginx, when checking for the log files, I get a hit on access.log:

Maybe log poisoning is possible? Since the log file is huge. I performed a reset on the box.

After the successful reset, I poisoned the access.log file and placed my simple PHP web shell inside the User-Agent field:

And using the poisoned log file, I achieved command execution:

Using the same method, I achieved a reverse shell connection. The entire Burp Suite request is the following:
